senses.title: The academic study of the economy
senses.titleCN: 经济学：研究经济活动的学科
senses.definition: the social science that studies how goods, services and money are produced, distributed and consumed
senses.definitionCN: 研究商品、服务与货币如何被生产、分配和消费的社会科学
senses.example: Economics explains why prices rise when supply falls.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学解释了供给下降时价格为何上涨。
senses.why: The Greek root named household management, and -ics marks a field of study, so economics is the discipline built around that management.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「管理家户」，-ics 标记一门学科，因此 economics 就是围绕这种管理建立起来的学问。

senses.title: The economic state of a place
senses.titleCN: 经济状况：某地的经济情况
senses.definition: the financial condition and performance of a country, region or industry
senses.definitionCN: 国家、地区或行业在财政上的状况与表现
senses.example: The report describes the economics of the fishing towns on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告描述了沿海渔镇的经济状况。
senses.why: The discipline name shifted onto its own subject matter: what the subject studies can also be called its economics.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称移到了它所研究的对象上：这门学问研究的东西，也可以被称为它的 economics。

senses.title: The cost-and-benefit calculation
senses.titleCN: 经济账：某项计划或交易的成本效益
senses.definition: the practical calculation of costs and returns in a particular plan, deal or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某项计划、交易或活动的成本与回报所作的实际核算
senses.example: The economics of the deal collapsed when fuel prices doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料价格翻倍后，这笔交易的经济账就算不过来了。
senses.why: A household manager weighs cost against return, and this everyday calculation is the practical echo of the academic subject.
senses.whyCN: 当家人要权衡成本与回报，这种日常核算就是这门学科在实务中的回声。

intro.en: Economics is a learned Greek compound whose English name for the discipline dates only from the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: economics 是学术性的希腊语复合词，它作为学科名称在英语中出现仅始于十九世纪。

items.en: Oikos meant house or household, the unit within which resources were managed.
items.cn: oikos 意为房子、家户，是资源被管理的单位。

items.en: Nomos meant law, rule or custom, giving oikonomia the sense of household rule.
items.cn: nomos 意为法律、规则或习俗，使 oikonomia 带上「家户规则」的意思。

items.en: Oikonomia covered household management and later public finance.
items.cn: oikonomia 涵盖家务管理，后来也指公共财政。

items.en: Latin carried the word into European learning, where it still meant management rather than a market system.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词带入欧洲学术，当时它仍指管理，而不是市场体系。

items.en: Political economy was shortened to economics as a name for the new university discipline; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着新的大学学科成形，political economy 被缩为 economics；确切首次使用年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the four words most often confused in this family; the near-meaning group gathers names for financial study and practice.
note.cn: 形近组收这一词族中最常被混淆的四个词；近义组收表示金融研究与实务的名称。

entries.definitionCN: 对金钱的研究与管理，尤指公共或公司层面。

entries.definitionCN: 对财务账目进行记录与核对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the discipline, its subject matter and its practical calculation in three separate boxes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把「学科」「研究对象」与「实际核算」分放在三个盒子里。

normal.en: Economics with -ics is the classroom; economy without it is the world outside.
normal.cn: 带 -ics 的 economics 是课堂；去掉它的 economy 是课堂外的世界。

normal.en: The same word can mean the subject, the condition it studies, or the sum done on a deal.
normal.cn: 同一个词可以指学科、它所研究的状况，或一笔交易上的算式。

normal.en: Oikos plus nomos: a house plus a rule, scaled up to a nation.
normal.cn: oikos 加 nomos：一所房子加一条规则，再放大到一个国家。

normal.en: The economics of a deal is a small household sum written large.
normal.cn: 一笔交易的 economics，就是放大写出的家常账。

normal.en: An economist is the person, economics is the field: one suffix marks the other's practitioner.
normal.cn: economist 是人，economics 是领域：一个后缀标出另一个的从业者。

abstract.en: The same crossing can stand for a theory, a country's condition, or a deal that no longer pays.
abstract.cn: 同一个交点可以代表一套理论、一个国家的状况，或一笔不再划算的交易。

abstract.en: Economics means the rules of the house, studied and applied.
abstract.cn: economics 意味着「家户的规则」，既被研究，也被应用。

senses.title: The system of production and trade
senses.titleCN: 经济体系：一国生产与贸易的系统
senses.definition: the system by which a country or region produces, distributes and consumes goods, services and money
senses.definitionCN: 国家或地区生产、分配与消费商品、服务和货币的系统
senses.example: The economy slowed after the harvest failed.
senses.exampleCN: 收成失败后经济放缓。
senses.why: The Greek word first meant household management; as states took on the same task, the word grew to name a whole national system.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词起初表示家务管理；当国家承担同样的任务，这个词就扩大为指整个国家系统。

senses.title: Careful use of resources
senses.definition: the careful avoidance of waste in money, fuel, time or materials
senses.definitionCN: 在金钱、燃料、时间或材料上谨慎避免浪费
senses.example: The office introduced an economy of paper and ink.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室推行了纸张与墨水的节约措施。
senses.why: The older household sense survives here: a good manager wastes little, and that habit is itself called economy.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的家户义在这里留存：好当家人很少浪费，而这种习惯本身就叫 economy。

senses.title: A saving made
senses.definition: a specific saving or reduction in spending, often plural as economies
senses.definitionCN: 具体的一笔节省或开支削减，常用复数 economies
senses.example: The new heating system brought real economies in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 新的供暖系统在冬天带来了实实在在的节省。
senses.why: A habit of thrift produces concrete results, and each result is an economy rather than the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 节俭的习惯会产生具体结果，每一个结果都是一项 economy，而不是习惯本身。

senses.title: The cheapest travel class
senses.titleCN: 经济舱：最便宜的出行等级
senses.definition: the cheapest class of seating on an aircraft or train, or the lowest grade of service
senses.definitionCN: 飞机或火车上最便宜的座位等级，或最低档次的服务
senses.example: She flew economy and spent the saving on a better hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐经济舱，把省下的钱花在更好的酒店上。
senses.why: Airlines borrowed the thrift sense: economy class is the class chosen to spend little.
senses.whyCN: 航空公司借用了「节俭」义：经济舱就是为少花钱而选的舱位。

intro.en: Economy is older in English than economics, and it reached the meaning of a national system only in the modern period.

items.en: Latin kept the sense of management, including the management of public revenue.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留「管理」义，也包括公共收入的管理。

items.en: Economy entered English as the management of a household or establishment.
items.cn: economy 进入英语时指家户或机构的管理。

items.en: The word was applied to the resources of a state, and the national sense became dominant.
items.cn: 这个词被用到国家的资源上，「国民经济」义逐渐占据主导。

items.en: Thrift, savings and travel class followed as narrower everyday uses of the same idea.
items.cn: 节俭、节省与舱位等级随后作为同一想法的日常窄义出现。

normal.en: Economy is the thing itself; economics is the study of the thing.
normal.cn: economy 是事物本身，economics 是对这事物的研究。

normal.en: A household that wastes nothing is the small model of a national economy.
normal.cn: 一个不浪费的家户，就是国民经济的小模型。

normal.en: One saving is an economy; many savings are economies.
normal.cn: 一笔节省是一项 economy；许多笔就是 economies。

normal.en: Chemists speak of economy of effort, drivers of fuel economy: thrift applied to a resource.
normal.cn: 化学家说 economy of effort，司机说 fuel economy：都是把节俭用到某种资源上。

normal.en: A false economy costs more later than it saves now.
normal.cn: a false economy 现在省下的，日后要花更多。

abstract.en: The same threads can be pulled tight by thrift, or cut into a ticket class.

abstract.en: Economy means a managed whole, whether a country, a budget or a seat.
abstract.cn: economy 意味着一个被管理的整体，无论国家、预算还是一个座位。

senses.title: The outer limit of a surface
senses.definition: the line or area where a surface ends and something else begins
senses.definitionCN: 一个表面结束、另一事物开始的界线或区域
senses.example: He stood at the edge of the cliff and looked down.
senses.exampleCN: 他站在悬崖边，向下看。
senses.why: Old English ecg named both the border and the blade, because a blade is the very edge of a tool.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ecg 同时指边界与刀刃，因为刀刃正是一件工具最外的那条边。

senses.title: The cutting side of a blade
senses.definition: the sharp side of a knife, axe or other cutting tool
senses.definitionCN: 刀、斧或其他切割工具上锋利的那一侧
senses.example: The axe had a chip on its edge after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，斧刃上崩了一个口。
senses.why: The same word covers border and blade because the cutting part is the boundary of the metal itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词兼指边界与刀刃，因为切割的部分正是金属自身的边界。

senses.title: An advantage over others
senses.definition: a small advantage that makes one person or group likely to win
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某群体更可能获胜的一点优势
senses.example: Years of night races gave her an edge on the track.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的夜间比赛让她在赛道上占了优势。
senses.why: To be at the edge is to be one step ahead of the rest, and a step ahead is an advantage.
senses.whyCN: 处在边缘就是比别人靠前一步，而靠前一步就是优势。

senses.title: A sharp or tense quality
senses.titleCN: 尖锐：声音或情绪的锋利感；紧张
senses.definition: a sharp, angry or nervous quality in a voice, mood or atmosphere, as in on edge
senses.definitionCN: 声音、情绪或气氛中的尖锐、恼怒或紧张，如短语 on edge
senses.example: There was an edge in his voice that worried everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他声音里有一股尖锐，让大家都担心起来。
senses.why: A blade's edge cuts, so a mood with an edge is a mood that can cut into others.
senses.whyCN: 刀刃的 edge 会割人，所以带着 edge 的情绪就是一种会割到别人的情绪。

senses.title: To move gradually
senses.definition: to move slowly and carefully in small steps, or to move something that way
senses.definitionCN: 以小步缓慢小心地移动，或以同样方式移动某物
senses.example: She edged the chair toward the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她把椅子一点点挪向窗边。
senses.why: Moving along the edge of a thing is slow and cautious, so the verb took the sense of gradual movement.
senses.whyCN: 沿着某物的边缘移动既慢又小心，于是动词取得了「渐进移动」的意思。

intro.en: Edge is a native Old English word that named a border and a blade at once, and the advantage sense is much later.
intro.cn: edge 是古英语本族词，同时指边界与刀刃，而「优势」义出现得晚得多。

items.en: A root connected with sharpness or a cutting point is sometimes proposed, but the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 有时会提出一个与「锋利、切割点」有关的词根，但重构结果不确定。

items.en: A Germanic noun for edge or blade is reconstructed and survives in several languages.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「边缘、刀刃」的日耳曼语名词，并在多种语言中留存。

items.en: Ecg meant edge, border and sword-blade, already joining the three ideas.
items.cn: ecg 意为边缘、边界与剑刃，当时已把三种意思合在一起。

items.en: The word settled into the modern spelling and added the sense of a boundary in space or time.
items.cn: 这个词固定为现代拼写，并加入「空间或时间边界」的意思。

items.en: The advantage and nervous-tension senses came from sport and from the image of a cutting mood.
items.cn: 优势义与紧张义分别来自体育运动与「锋利情绪」的意象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for borders, blades and advantages.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收表示边界、刀刃与优势的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning nervous, tense or stylistically sharp.

entries.definition: A border or trim along an edge.
entries.definitionCN: 沿边缘的饰边或镶边。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning sideways, or on edge.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「侧着地」或「沿边地」。

entries.definition: The line dividing two areas or countries.
entries.definitionCN: 划分两个地区或国家的界线。

entries.definition: The flat cutting part of a knife or tool.
entries.definitionCN: 刀或工具上扁平的切割部分。

entries.definition: A condition that puts one in a better position.
entries.definitionCN: 使人处于更有利地位的条件。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run along a cliff edge, then along a blade, then toward advantage and tension.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子先沿悬崖边缘走，再沿刀刃走，最后走向优势与紧张。

normal.en: Edge is a line where one thing stops and another begins.
normal.cn: edge 是一条线，在那里一件事结束，另一件事开始。

normal.en: A blade is the edge of the metal, so knife and border share one word.
normal.cn: 刀刃就是金属的边，所以刀与边界共用一个词。

normal.en: One step past the edge is one step ahead of the crowd.
normal.cn: 越过边缘一步，就是领先人群一步。

normal.en: A voice with an edge can cut, just as a blade can.
normal.cn: 带 edge 的嗓音会割人，就像刀刃一样。

normal.en: To edge forward is to move as if along a cliff: small, careful steps.
normal.cn: edge forward 就是像沿悬崖那样移动：小步、小心。

abstract.en: Picture a boot toe exactly on a chalk line at the lip of a drop.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞋尖正好停在悬崖边的一条粉笔线上。

abstract.en: The same line can be a cliff, a knife, a scoreboard or a tone of voice.
abstract.cn: 同一条线可以是悬崖、刀刃、记分牌或说话的腔调。

abstract.en: Edge means the place where position becomes decisive.
abstract.cn: edge 意味着位置变得具有决定性的那个地方。

examples.en: He stood at the edge of the cliff and looked down.
examples.cn: 他站在悬崖边，向下看。

examples.en: Years of night races gave her an edge on the track.
examples.cn: 多年的夜间比赛让她在赛道上占了优势。

examples.en: She edged the chair toward the window.
examples.cn: 她把椅子一点点挪向窗边。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of edge: a boundary in space, the boundary of a blade, a step ahead of others, a cutting tone, and a cautious movement.
sensesIntro.cn: edge 的五个义项：空间边界、刀刃的边界、领先他人的一步、割人的腔调，以及小心的移动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boot toe stops exactly on a chalk line at the lip of a drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：鞋尖正好停在悬崖边的一条粉笔线上。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the line where a surface or area ends.
branches.cn: 边界线：表面或区域结束的那条线。

branches.en: THE BLADE: the sharp boundary of a cutting tool.
branches.cn: 刀刃线：切割工具锋利的边界。

branches.en: THE ADVANTAGE: being one step past the others.
branches.cn: 优势线：比别人多走一步。

branches.cn: 紧张线：会割人的嗓音或情绪。

branches.en: THE MOTION: moving as if along a cliff, in small steps.
branches.cn: 移动线：像沿悬崖那样小步移动。

intro.cn: edge 是古英语本族词，英语加后缀与复合成分，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no part in this word; the learned synonym acies belongs to a different tradition.

senses.title: A version of a published work
senses.titleCN: 版本：同一作品的一次出版形式
senses.definition: a particular form in which a book, magazine or other work is published, differing from other forms in content, size or cover
senses.definitionCN: 书、杂志或其他作品出版时的一种具体形式，在内容、开本或封面上与其他形式不同
senses.example: The first edition sold out within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 第一版一周内售罄。
senses.why: Latin editio meant a bringing forth; a version is what a publisher brings out at one moment, with its own text and shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 editio 意为「拿出、产出」；版本就是出版者在某一时刻拿出来的东西，有自己的文本与形态。

senses.title: One print run
senses.definition: the whole number of copies of a work printed and issued at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次印刷并发行的一件作品的全部册数
senses.example: The library bought the entire edition of the new atlas.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆买下了新地图册的整版印量。
senses.why: The act of bringing forth produces a batch, and the batch itself took the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 「拿出」这一动作会产生一批东西，而这一批东西本身就沿用了动作的名称。

senses.title: A regular version of a broadcast
senses.titleCN: 一期：定期出版或播出的一个版本
senses.definition: one of the regular forms of a newspaper, programme or broadcast, such as an evening edition
senses.definitionCN: 报纸、节目或广播的常规形式之一，如晚报版
senses.example: The evening edition carries the closing stock prices.
senses.exampleCN: 晚报版刊登收盘股价。
senses.why: A daily paper brings forth a new version each day, so each issue is another edition of the same title.
senses.whyCN: 日报每天拿出一个新版本，所以每一期都是同一报名下的又一次 edition。

intro.en: Edition comes from Latin verbs of giving out, and its whole family is built on the idea of bringing something forth.
intro.cn: edition 来自拉丁语中「拿出、发出」的动词，整个词族都围绕「把东西拿出来」这一想法。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and it supplied the second element of the publishing verbs.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，为出版类动词提供第二个成分。

items.en: E plus dare formed edere, 'to give out, bring forth, publish'.
items.cn: e- 加 dare 构成 edere，意为「发出、拿出、出版」。

items.en: Editio was the noun of that act, a bringing forth or a publication.
items.cn: editio 是这一动作的名词，意为「拿出、出版」。

items.en: French passed the word to English, where it narrowed to a published version.
items.cn: 法语把这个词传给英语，在英语中窄化为「已出版的版本」。

items.en: Printing and broadcasting added the senses of a print run and a regular issue.
items.cn: 印刷与广播又加入了「印量」与「定期一期」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the publishing family; the near-meaning group gathers words for versions and copies.
note.cn: 形近组收出版词族；近义组收表示版本与册本的词。

entries.definition: A person who prepares text or a publication for issue.
entries.definitionCN: 为出版而整理文本或出版物的人。

entries.definition: An adjective for editing, or a newspaper's opinion article.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指编辑的；也指报纸的评论文章。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to prepare or correct text, film or sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为编辑或剪辑文本、影像与声音。

entries.definition: A form of something that differs from other forms of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与同一事物的其他形式有所不同的一个形式。

entries.definition: One number of a magazine or newspaper, or a set of items issued together.
entries.definitionCN: 杂志或报纸的一期，或一起发行的一套物品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a stack of covers to one print run and then to the evening paper.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一摞封面，走到一次印量，再到晚报。

normal.en: Edition is a bringing forth: the publisher brings a version out.
normal.cn: edition 就是「拿出来」：出版者把一个版本拿出来。

normal.en: Same title, different cover: that is a new edition, not a new book.
normal.cn: 同一书名，不同封面：那是新版本，不是新书。

normal.en: One printing makes one edition, counted in copies.
normal.cn: 一次印刷构成一个版次，以册数计算。

normal.en: A daily paper is a new edition every day, which is why we say evening edition.
normal.cn: 日报每天都是新的一版，所以我们说 evening edition。

normal.en: Edition, editor and edit all come from the same giving-out verb.
normal.cn: edition、editor、edit 都来自同一个表示「拿出」的动词。

abstract.en: Picture several stacks of one book, each cover a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象同一本书的几摞，每摞封面颜色不同。

abstract.en: The same stack can be a revised text, a print run, or today's paper.
abstract.cn: 同一摞书可以是一个修订文本、一次印量，或今天的报纸。

abstract.en: Edition means the same work put out again in a new form.
abstract.cn: edition 意味着同一作品以新形态再次出版。

sensesIntro.cn: edition 的三个义项：作品的一种版本、一次印刷的册数，以及报纸或节目的一期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several stacks of one book, each with a differently coloured cover.

branches.cn: 批次线：版本以实际印出的册数而存在。

senses.title: A person who prepares text
senses.definition: a person whose job is to prepare written material for publication by correcting, cutting and arranging it
senses.definitionCN: 以修改、删减和编排书面材料来准备出版为职业的人
senses.example: The editor cut a whole paragraph before the issue closed.
senses.exampleCN: 截稿前编辑删掉了整整一段。
senses.why: Latin editor meant one who brings forth; the modern editor brings a text out into the world in its final shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 editor 意为「把东西拿出来的人」；现代编辑就是把文本以最终形态带到世人面前的人。

senses.title: The person in charge of a publication
senses.titleCN: 主编：负责一份出版物的人
senses.definition: the senior person who decides what a newspaper, magazine or series will contain
senses.definitionCN: 决定报纸、杂志或丛书内容的资深负责人
senses.example: The editor refused to print the story without a second source.
senses.exampleCN: 没有第二个消息来源，主编拒绝刊登这篇报道。
senses.why: Bringing forth a paper belongs to the person at the top of the desk, so editor also names the post of command.
senses.whyCN: 把一份报纸拿出来，是编辑部最高负责人的职责，于是 editor 也指这个指挥职位。

senses.title: A person who cuts film or sound
senses.titleCN: 剪辑师：剪辑影像或声音的人
senses.definition: a person who selects and arranges shots, scenes or sound recordings for a film, video or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 为电影、视频或广播挑选与编排镜头、场景或录音的人
senses.example: The film editor built the chase from forty separate shots.
senses.exampleCN: 剪辑师用四十个独立镜头剪出了这场追逐。
senses.why: Film is brought forth by cutting and joining, so the worker who does that keeps the old title of one who brings forth.

intro.en: Editor is Latin in form and meaning: one who brings something forth for others.
intro.cn: editor 的形态与含义都来自拉丁语：把某物拿出来给别人的人。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and it is the second element of the publishing verb.

items.en: E plus dare formed edere, to give out or bring forth.
items.cn: e- 加 dare 构成 edere，意为「发出、拿出」。

items.en: Editor was the person noun for one who brings forth or publishes.
items.cn: editor 是表示「拿出者、出版者」的指人名词。

items.en: English borrowed editor for a publisher or writer, and the word later narrowed to the person who prepares text.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 editor，指出版者或作者，后来窄化为整理文本的人。

items.en: Newspapers and film added the commanding and the cutting senses, while the root meaning stayed visible.

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the publishing family; the near-meaning group gathers people who work on texts and images.
note.cn: 形近组收出版词族；近义组收处理文本与影像的人。

entries.definition: One published version or print run of a work.

entries.definition: An adjective for editing, or a newspaper's opinion piece.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指编辑的；也指报纸评论文章。

entries.definition: The position or period of being an editor.
entries.definitionCN: 编辑的职位或任期。

entries.definition: A person who checks text for errors before printing.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷前检查文本错误的人。

entries.definition: A person who gathers news for a paper or broadcast.
entries.definitionCN: 为报纸或广播采集新闻的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the person who brings text, papers and films out into the world.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着那个把文本、报纸与电影带到世人面前的人。

normal.en: Editor means one who brings forth; the red pen is the tool of bringing forth.
normal.cn: editor 意为「拿出者」；红笔就是拿出的工具。

normal.en: The editor-in-chief brings out the whole paper, not one page.
normal.cn: 主编拿出的是整份报纸，而不是一页。

normal.en: A film editor brings out a story by choosing which shots survive.
normal.cn: 电影剪辑师通过决定哪些镜头存活，把一个故事拿出来。

normal.en: Edit, editor, edition, editorial: one giving-out family.
normal.cn: edit、editor、edition、editorial：同一个「拿出」词族。

normal.en: A copy editor saves the reader from the writer's mistakes.
normal.cn: 文字编辑替读者挡住作者的错。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting a clean page out of a pile of marked drafts.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从一摞批注稿中抽出一张干净的纸。

abstract.en: The same lifting can produce a book, a newspaper, a film, or a corrected paragraph.
abstract.cn: 同一次「抽出」可以产出一本书、一份报纸、一部电影，或一个改好的段落。

abstract.en: Editor means someone decides what version of a thing the world will see.

root: 拉丁语 editor「拿出者、出版者」由 edere「发出、出版」派生，edere 又由 e-「出」加 dare「给」构成；十七世纪进入英语，后窄化为整理文本的人。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of editor: the person who prepares text, the person in charge of a publication, and the person who cuts film or sound.
sensesIntro.cn: editor 的三个义项：整理文本的人、负责一份出版物的人，以及剪辑影像或声音的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifts one clean page out of a pile of marked drafts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从一摞批注稿中抽出一张干净的纸。

branches.en: THE TEXT: correcting and arranging words for publication.
branches.cn: 文本线：为出版而修改与编排文字。

branches.en: THE DESK: deciding what a whole publication contains.
branches.cn: 编辑部线：决定整份出版物的内容。

branches.en: THE CUT: choosing which shots or sounds survive.
branches.cn: 剪辑线：决定哪些镜头或声音留存。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: the same person may both polish the text and command the desk.
branches.cn: 权威线：同一个人可能既打磨文本又指挥编辑部。

branches.en: THE SELECTION: in words and in film, the job is choosing what to keep.
branches.cn: 取舍线：无论文字还是电影，这份工作都是决定留下什么。

intro.en: Editor is a Latin agent noun; English adds -ial, -ship and plural endings.
intro.cn: editor 是拉丁语施事名词，英语加 -ial、-ship 与复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin edere and editor are recorded, and the agent suffix -or is visible in both Latin and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 edere 与 editor 均有记录，施事后缀 -or 在拉丁语与英语中都可见。

definition_en: a newspaper article giving the paper's opinion, or an adjective meaning relating to editing or expressing an opinion
core_image: 社论版上只有一篇未署名的长文
scene: 社论版上只有一篇未署名的长文。The editorial argued for a new bridge across the river.
sceneCN: 这里 editorial 是「社论」（第 1 个义项：报纸表达立场的评论文章）；句意为这篇社论主张在河上新建一座桥。图中可辨识物件：社论版、未署名长文、桥的插图。

形容词：编辑的；编辑上的；表达意见的

senses.title: A newspaper's opinion article
senses.titleCN: 社论：报纸表达立场的文章
senses.definition: a long article in a newspaper that gives the paper's own opinion on an important subject, usually without a named writer
senses.definitionCN: 报纸上就重要议题表达报社自身立场的长文，通常不署名
senses.example: The editorial argued for a new bridge across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇社论主张在河上新建一座桥。
senses.why: An opinion piece is written by the editorial desk rather than a reporter, so it took the adjective of that desk as its name.
senses.whyCN: 评论文章由编辑部而非记者撰写，于是它把「编辑部」的形容词拿来当名字。

senses.title: Relating to editing
senses.titleCN: 编辑的：与编辑工作有关
senses.definition: relating to the work of an editor, or to the preparation and correction of text
senses.definitionCN: 与编辑的工作有关，或与文本的准备和修改有关
senses.example: The editorial process took three weeks for a forty-page report.
senses.exampleCN: 一份四十页的报告，编辑流程走了三周。
senses.why: This is the plain adjective from editor: whatever belongs to the editor's work is editorial.
senses.whyCN: 这是 editor 的普通形容词：凡属于编辑工作的都是 editorial。

senses.title: Expressing an opinion
senses.titleCN: 表达意见的：带评论立场的
senses.definition: expressing a judgement or opinion rather than reporting plain facts
senses.definitionCN: 表达判断或意见，而非只报道事实
senses.example: The magazine added an editorial note beside the disputed figure.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志在有争议的数据旁加了一条评论性按语。
senses.why: The opinion article gave the word this colouring: editorial comment is comment that takes a side.
senses.whyCN: 社论赋予这个词这种色彩：editorial comment 就是选边站的评论。

intro.en: Editorial is a derived adjective that became a noun when newspapers needed a name for their own voice.
intro.cn: editorial 本是派生形容词，当报纸需要为自己的声音命名时，它又成了名词。

items.en: Editor meant one who brings forth or publishes, the base of the English word.
items.cn: editor 意为「拿出者、出版者」，是英语词的词基。

items.en: The adjective suffix -ial formed editorial, meaning belonging to an editor or to editing.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -ial 构成 editorial，意为「属于编辑或编辑工作的」。

items.en: The adjective spread in printing and publishing, and American papers began using it for opinion articles.
items.cn: 这个形容词在印刷与出版业传播，美国报纸开始用它指评论文章。

items.en: Editorial as a noun settled on the unsigned statement of a paper's view; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 作为名词的 editorial 固定在报纸不署名的立场声明上；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Broadcasting and online media extended editorial to any comment that takes a side.
items.cn: 广播与网络媒体把 editorial 扩展到任何选边站的评论。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers editing-family words; the near-meaning group gathers opinion writing and comment.
note.cn: 形近组收编辑词族；近义组收意见写作与评论。

entries.definition: A person who prepares text, a paper or a film.
entries.definitionCN: 整理文本、报纸或电影的人。

entries.definition: A published version or one print run.
entries.definitionCN: 一种出版版本或一次印量。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in an editorial way or in editorial terms.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以社论方式」或「在编辑层面」。

entries.definition: A regular signed article in a paper expressing a writer's view.
entries.definitionCN: 报纸上由署名人定期撰写、表达其观点的文章。

entries.definition: Explanation or opinion about events, often broadcast or written alongside them.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的解释或意见，常与事件同时播出或刊出。

normalIntro.en: These hooks go from the unsigned page to the editing process and then to any comment that takes a side.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从不署名的版面，走到编辑流程，再到任何选边站的评论。

normal.en: An editorial is the newspaper speaking in its own voice, with no byline.
normal.cn: 社论是报纸用自己的声音说话，不署名。

normal.en: Editorial work is what happens before the text becomes public.
normal.cn: 编辑工作发生在文本公开之前。

normal.en: An editorial note does not just report; it judges.
normal.cn: 评论性按语不只是报道，它还下判断。

normal.en: The editorial board is the room where that voice is decided.
normal.cn: 社论委员会就是决定这个声音的那间屋子。

normal.en: Editorial the noun and editorial the adjective differ only in function.
normal.cn: 名词 editorial 与形容词 editorial 只差功能，不差词根。

abstract.en: Picture a page with one long unsigned column and no advertisements.
abstract.cn: 想象一页只有一篇未署名长文，没有广告。

abstract.en: The same page can be a paper's opinion, a magazine's note, or a broadcast comment.
abstract.cn: 同一页可以是一家报纸的立场、一本杂志的按语，或一段广播评论。

abstract.en: Editorial means the institution itself is doing the talking.
abstract.cn: editorial 意味着说话的是机构本身。

examples.en: The editorial argued for a new bridge across the river.
examples.cn: 这篇社论主张在河上新建一座桥。

examples.en: The editorial process took three weeks for a forty-page report.
examples.cn: 一份四十页的报告，编辑流程走了三周。

examples.en: The magazine added an editorial note beside the disputed figure.
examples.cn: 杂志在有争议的数据旁加了一条评论性按语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of editorial: the paper's own opinion article, anything belonging to editing, and comment that takes a side.
sensesIntro.cn: editorial 的三个义项：报纸自身的评论文章、属于编辑工作的事物，以及选边站的评论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page holding one long unsigned column and no advertisements.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页只有一篇未署名长文，没有广告。

branches.en: THE ARTICLE: the paper's own opinion, printed without a byline.
branches.cn: 文章线：报纸自身的立场，刊登时不署名。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: everything that belongs to preparing text for publication.
branches.cn: 流程线：一切属于准备文本出版的工作。

branches.en: THE STANCE: comment that judges rather than merely reports.
branches.cn: 立场线：作判断而不只是报道的评论。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the article and the note both speak for someone.
branches.cn: 声音线：社论与按语都在替某一方说话。

branches.en: THE FILTER: editing decides what reaches the public and in what tone.
branches.cn: 过滤线：编辑决定什么以何种语气到达公众。

intro.en: Editorial is transparently editor plus -ial; English adds an adverb ending to it.
intro.cn: editorial 的构造一目了然：editor 加 -ial，英语再给它加副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The base editor is recorded Latin; the suffix -ial continues a Latin adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 editor 是有记录的拉丁语；后缀 -ial 延续拉丁语形容词词尾。

definition_zh: 教育；培养；训练；向公众宣传
definition_en: to teach someone over time, to develop their abilities and judgement, or to inform the public about something
core_image: 老师把一张地图挂上墙，孩子们围过来找河流
scene: 教室里老师把一张地图挂上墙，让孩子们找河流。Teachers educate children in both reading and judgment.
sceneCN: 这里 educate 是「教育、培养」（第 1 个义项：长期教导并发展能力）；句意为教师既教孩子读书，也教他们判断。图中可辨识物件：地图、教室、围过来的孩子。

pos.zh: 动词：教育；培养；训练；向公众宣传

collocations.zh: 向公众宣传；提高公众认识

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「教育」

senses.title: To teach and develop a person
senses.titleCN: 教育：教导并发展一个人
senses.definition: to teach a person over a period of time, developing knowledge, skills and judgement
senses.definitionCN: 在较长时期内教导一个人，发展其知识、技能与判断力
senses.example: Teachers educate children in both reading and judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 教师既教孩子读书，也教他们判断。
senses.why: Latin educare meant to rear or bring up, so the verb is about raising a whole person rather than delivering a fact.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 educare 意为「养育、抚养」，所以这个动词关乎养大一个完整的人，而不是交付一个事实。

senses.title: To inform the public
senses.definition: to give people information about an issue so that they can understand it and act sensibly
senses.definitionCN: 向人们提供某议题的信息，使其能够理解并合理行动
senses.example: The campaign educates farmers about safer ways to store grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这项运动向农民宣传更安全的储粮方法。
senses.why: Bringing up a person is close to bringing them out of ignorance, so educate also means informing a public that lacks a fact.
senses.whyCN: 养大一个人与把他带出无知很接近，所以 educate 也指向缺乏某事实的公众提供信息。

senses.title: To train a skill or sense
senses.titleCN: 训练：培养某种技能或感官
senses.definition: to train a particular ability, such as the ear, the eye or the taste, through practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过练习培养某种能力，如听力、眼力或品味
senses.example: Years of listening educated her ear for tiny changes in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的聆听训练了她对细微音调变化的听力。
senses.why: Development is not only academic, so the same verb covers the training of a single faculty.
senses.whyCN: 发展不只发生在学业上，因此同一个动词也涵盖单一官能的训练。

intro.en: Educate comes from a Latin verb for rearing, and its link with the 'lead out' verb has been debated for centuries.
intro.cn: educate 来自一个表示「养育」的拉丁动词，它同「引出」动词的联系已争论数百年。

items.en: Educare meant to bring up, rear or nourish a child, and it is the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: educare 意为抚养、养育、培育孩子，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: A similar verb educere meant to lead out; many writers link education to leading a mind out, but the two verbs are not certainly the same.
items.cn: 一个形近动词 educere 意为「引出」；许多作者把教育联系到「把心智引出来」，但两个动词未必同源。

items.en: The noun educatio named the rearing and training of a child.
items.cn: 名词 educatio 指对孩子的养育与训练。

items.en: English borrowed the verb, first in the sense of rearing and then in the sense of formal teaching.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，先有「养育」义，后有「正式教学」义。

items.en: Public campaigns and self-improvement added the senses of informing the public and training a faculty.
items.cn: 公共宣传与自我提升又加入了「告知公众」与「训练官能」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the education family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for teaching and training.
note.cn: 形近组收教育词族；近义组收表示教导与训练的动词。

entries.definition: The process or system of teaching, or the knowledge gained.
entries.definitionCN: 教学的过程或制度，或由此获得的知识。

entries.definition: A person who teaches or works in education.
entries.definitionCN: 从事教学或教育工作的人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to education or instructive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的」或「有教育意义的」。

entries.definition: To give lessons or instruction in a subject or skill.
entries.definitionCN: 就某一科目或技能授课或指导。

entries.definition: To practise a skill until it becomes reliable.
entries.definitionCN: 反复练习某项技能直到稳定可靠。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from raising a child, to informing a public, to training one sharp sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从养大一个孩子，走到告知公众，再到训练一种敏锐的官能。

normal.en: Educate is first a feeding word: it meant to rear a child.
normal.cn: educate 起初是「喂养」类词：意为养大一个孩子。

normal.en: A teacher educates by developing judgement, not by filling a memory.
normal.cn: 教师通过发展判断力来 educate，而不是填满记忆。

normal.en: A public campaign educates when people can act on what they learn.
normal.cn: 当人们能依所学行动时，公共宣传才真正 educate。

normal.en: An educated ear can hear what an untrained ear misses.
normal.cn: 受过训练的耳朵能听见未训练者漏掉的东西。

normal.en: An educated guess is a guess with schooling behind it.
normal.cn: an educated guess 是有学识在背后支撑的猜测。

abstract.en: Picture a hand drawing a child forward, one step at a time, over many years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在多年里一步一步把孩子往前带。

abstract.en: The same pulling forward can apply to a pupil, a village or one sense.
abstract.cn: 同一种「往前带」可以用在学生、一个村庄，或一种官能上。

abstract.en: Educate means the person can now do what they could not do before.
abstract.cn: educate 意味着这个人如今能做到从前做不到的事。

examples.en: Teachers educate children in both reading and judgment.
examples.cn: 教师既教孩子读书，也教他们判断。

examples.en: The campaign educates farmers about safer ways to store grain.
examples.cn: 这项运动向农民宣传更安全的储粮方法。

examples.en: Years of listening educated her ear for tiny changes in tone.
examples.cn: 多年的聆听训练了她对细微音调变化的听力。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of educate: raising a whole person, informing a public, and training a single ability.
sensesIntro.cn: educate 的三个义项：养大一个完整的人、告知公众，以及训练单一能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand draws a child forward over many years, one step at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在多年里一步一步把孩子往前带。

branches.en: THE PERSON: long-term teaching that forms knowledge, skill and judgement.
branches.cn: 人物线：长期教学，形成知识、技能与判断力。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC: giving people the facts they need to act.
branches.cn: 公众线：给人们行动所需的事实。

branches.en: THE FACULTY: practising one ability, such as the ear or the eye.
branches.cn: 官能线：反复练习一种能力，如耳或眼。

branches.en: THE GROWTH: a whole person and a single sense both grow by practice.
branches.cn: 成长线：完整的人与单一官能都靠练习成长。

branches.en: THE IGNORANCE: teaching and public information both remove a lack.
branches.cn: 无知线：教学与公共信息都在消除某种匮乏。

senses.title: The process or system of teaching
senses.titleCN: 教育：教与学的过程或制度
senses.definition: the process of teaching and learning, especially in schools, or the system that organizes it
senses.definitionCN: 教与学的过程，尤指学校中的过程，或组织这一过程的制度
senses.example: Education is compulsory until the age of sixteen here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里十六岁以前实行义务教育。
senses.why: Latin educatio named the rearing of a child, and the modern noun keeps that long, guided process rather than a single lesson.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 educatio 指养育孩子，现代名词保留的正是这种长期、被引导的过程，而不是一堂课。

senses.title: The knowledge gained
senses.titleCN: 受教育程度：获得的知识与素养
senses.definition: the knowledge, skills and understanding that a person has gained through learning
senses.definitionCN: 一个人通过学习获得的知识、技能与理解力
senses.example: She used her education to set up a village clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她用自己受过的教育办起了一所村诊所。
senses.why: The process leaves a result in the person, and the result is also called education.
senses.whyCN: 过程在人身上留下结果，而这一结果也被称为 education。

senses.title: The study of teaching
senses.titleCN: 教育学：研究教学的学科
senses.definition: the academic field that studies how people teach and learn
senses.definitionCN: 研究人们如何教与学的学术领域
senses.example: He took a degree in education before becoming a head teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他在成为校长之前读了教育学学位。
senses.why: Once teaching became an object of research, the name of the activity also named the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 当教学成为研究对象，这一活动的名称也就用来指研究它的学科。

intro.en: Education is the noun of the rearing verb, and its history runs from the family to the school and then to the university department.
intro.cn: education 是「养育」动词的名词，其历史从家庭走到学校，再走到大学系科。

items.en: Educare meant to rear or bring up a child, with the care and feeding that the image implies.
items.cn: educare 意为抚养、养育孩子，带有照料与喂养的意象。

items.en: Educatio named the rearing and training itself, not the person who did it.
items.cn: educatio 指养育与训练这件事本身，而不是做这件事的人。

items.en: English borrowed education for the process of rearing and instruction.
items.cn: 英语借入 education，指养育与教导的过程。

items.en: With public schooling, the word shifted toward organized teaching by the state.
items.cn: 随着公共教育兴起，这个词转向国家组织的有计划教学。

items.en: The knowledge sense and the academic-discipline sense completed the modern range.
items.cn: 「知识」义与「学科」义补全了现代用法范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the teaching family; the near-meaning group gathers words for learning, schooling and instruction.
note.cn: 形近组收教学词族；近义组收表示学习、学校与教导的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to teach and develop a person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为教育与培养一个人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to education or instructive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的」或「有教育意义的」。

entries.definition: A person who studies or works in education.
entries.definitionCN: 研究教育或从事教育工作的人。

entries.definition: The education received at school, especially formal instruction.
entries.definitionCN: 在学校接受的教育，尤指正式教学。

entries.definition: Knowledge gained by study, or the process of gaining it.
entries.definitionCN: 通过学习获得的知识，或获得它的过程。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a timetable on a board to the knowledge in a person and then to the department that studies teaching.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从黑板上的课程表，走到一个人身上的知识，再到研究教学的系科。

normal.en: Education is the process first: a timetable, a classroom, a long sequence of years.
normal.cn: education 首先是过程：一张课程表、一间教室、一连串年份。

normal.en: The process leaves something behind, and that something is also education.
normal.cn: 过程会留下东西，而留下的东西也叫 education。

normal.en: When the process itself is studied, education becomes a university subject.
normal.cn: 当过程本身被研究，education 就成了一门大学学科。

normal.en: Physical education is education of the body, not of the timetable.
normal.cn: physical education 是身体的教育，不是课程表的教育。

normal.en: Educate is the act, education is the process and its result.
normal.cn: educate 是动作，education 是过程及其结果。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor of classroom doors, each opening onto a year.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的走廊，每扇教室门都通向一年。

abstract.en: The same corridor can be a compulsory system, a personal possession, or a field of research.
abstract.cn: 同一条走廊可以是一项义务制度、一个人的所有物，或一个研究领域。

abstract.en: Education means a society deliberately carrying its knowledge to the next person.
abstract.cn: education 意味着一个社会有意把知识交到下一个人手里。

examples.en: Education is compulsory until the age of sixteen here.
examples.cn: 这里十六岁以前实行义务教育。

examples.en: She used her education to set up a village clinic.
examples.cn: 她用自己受过的教育办起了一所村诊所。

examples.en: He took a degree in education before becoming a head teacher.
examples.cn: 他在成为校长之前读了教育学学位。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of education: the organized process, the knowledge it leaves in a person, and the academic study of teaching.
sensesIntro.cn: education 的三个义项：有组织的过程、它在人身上留下的知识，以及研究教学的学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long corridor of classroom doors, each opening onto a year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长长的走廊，每扇教室门都通向一年。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: teaching and learning organized over years.
branches.cn: 过程线：多年组织起来的教与学。

branches.en: THE RESULT: the knowledge and judgement a person now has.
branches.cn: 结果线：一个人如今拥有的知识与判断力。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the university study of how teaching works.
branches.cn: 学科线：大学里对教学如何运作的研究。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: the process exists to leave something in the person.
branches.cn: 传递线：过程存在，是为了在人身上留下东西。

branches.en: THE REFLECTION: a system and the study of that system share one name.
branches.cn: 反照线：一个制度与研究它的学问共用一个名称。

intro.en: Education is a Latin-derived noun; English builds adjectives, verbs and person nouns from the same stem.
intro.cn: education 是源自拉丁语的名词，英语由同一词干构成形容词、动词与指人名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin educare and educatio are recorded; the suffix -ation continues a Latin noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 educare 与 educatio 均有记录；后缀 -ation 延续拉丁语名词词尾。

senses.title: A result of a cause
senses.definition: a change or result that is produced by an action, event or cause
senses.definitionCN: 由某个行为、事件或原因所造成的变化或结果
senses.example: The medicine had no effect on the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药对退烧没有效果。
senses.why: Effect is Latin effectus, a thing done; a cause does something, and what it leaves behind is the effect.
senses.whyCN: effect 源自拉丁语 effectus，意为「做成之事」；原因做出某事，留在后面的东西就是结果。

senses.title: An impression on the senses
senses.definition: an impression produced on the eye, ear or mind, especially by light, sound or colour
senses.definitionCN: 尤指光线、声音或色彩在视觉、听觉或心理上造成的印象
senses.example: The film uses simple sound effects to build tension.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片用简单的音效营造紧张感。
senses.why: A stage light or a drumbeat does something to the audience, so the result it leaves in the senses is also an effect.
senses.whyCN: 舞台灯光或鼓点对观众做了某件事，于是在感官里留下的结果同样是一种 effect。

senses.title: The state of being in force
senses.definition: the state of being active or legally valid, as of a rule or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 规则或协议等处于运作或法律上有效的状态
senses.example: The new tax is now in effect.
senses.exampleCN: 新税现已生效。
senses.why: A law that has been made is a thing done; once it is in effect, that done thing stands and works.
senses.whyCN: 制定好的法律是一件「做成之事」；一旦 in effect，这件做成之事就立在那里并发挥作用。

senses.title: To bring something about
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or to bring it into being
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生或使其成为现实
senses.example: The manager effected a complete change of policy.
senses.exampleCN: 经理促成了政策的彻底改变。
senses.why: As a verb, effect names the act of doing the thing itself, not the result that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，effect 指「把这件事做出来」的动作本身，而不是随后留下的结果。

intro.en: Effect comes from Latin efficere, to do or bring about, through effectus, a thing done, and reached English by way of Old French.
intro.cn: effect 来自拉丁语 efficere（做出、完成），经分词 effectus（做成之事）与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make and supplied the core of the verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，提供这个动词的核心。

items.en: Ex- meaning out plus facere formed efficere, to work out or accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「做出来、完成」。

items.en: The participle effectus meant accomplished or brought about, and became a noun for the result.
items.cn: 分词 effectus 意为「已完成的、已做成的」，后来成为表示结果的名词。

items.en: Old French effect kept both the noun of result and the sense of accomplishment.
items.cn: 古法语 effect 同时保留了「结果」的名词义与「完成」的意味。

items.en: English first used it for a result and later for an impression and a rule in force.
items.cn: 英语先用它表示结果，后来扩展出感官印象与法规生效两义。

items.en: The verb use, to effect a change, settled beside the noun in formal style.
items.cn: 动词用法「促成一项改变」在正式文体中与名词用法并存固定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on effect and its easily confused partner affect; the near-meaning group separates result, consequence and impact.
note.cn: 形近组收由 effect 构成的词以及易混的 affect；近义组区分 result、consequence 与 impact。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to produce the wanted result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」，由 effect 加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a way that succeeds, or in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有效地、实际上」，由 effective 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to influence or to move emotionally; often confused with effect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响、使感动」，常与 effect 混淆。

entries.definition: Something that follows from an action; plainer and more general than effect.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，比 effect 更普通、更泛。

entries.definition: A result, often an indirect or unwelcome one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果」，常指间接或不受欢迎的结果。

entries.definition: A strong effect or influence on something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲击、重大影响」，强调力度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from one cause and follow its ripple outward into sensed impressions, standing laws and deliberate action.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一个原因出发，顺着涟漪走到感官印象、生效的法规与有意的行动。

normal.en: Effect is what a cause leaves behind.
normal.cn: effect 就是原因留在身后的东西。

normal.en: Sound effects are effects you hear, not results you measure.
normal.cn: sound effects 是你听见的效果，不是你去测量的结果。

normal.en: A rule in effect is a done thing still standing.
normal.cn: in effect 的规则就是一件做成之事仍立在那里。

normal.en: To effect a change is to do it; to affect something is to touch it.
normal.cn: to effect a change 是把它做出来；to affect 是触碰、影响它。

normal.en: Cause and effect are the two ends of one sentence.
normal.cn: 原因与结果是同一个句子的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水。

abstract.en: The same ripple can be seen, heard, or written into a law.
abstract.cn: 同一圈涟漪可以被看见、被听见，也可以被写进一条法律。

abstract.en: Effect is the mark left by something that acted.
abstract.cn: effect 就是某个东西行动之后留下的印记。

examples.en: The medicine had no effect on the fever.
examples.cn: 这种药对退烧没有效果。

examples.en: The film uses simple sound effects to build tension.
examples.cn: 这部影片用简单的音效营造紧张感。

examples.en: The manager effected a complete change of policy.
examples.cn: 经理促成了政策的彻底改变。

scene: 新规定贴出后，门口的长队当天就短了一半。The new rule proved effective from its first morning.

senses.title: Producing the wanted result
senses.definition: producing the result that was intended or wanted
senses.definitionCN: 能产生预期或想要的结果
senses.example: The vaccine is effective against the new strain.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗对新毒株有效。
senses.why: Effective adds -ive to effect: the thing has the power to leave the result you aimed at.
senses.whyCN: effective 是 effect 加 -ive：这件东西有能力留下你瞄准的那个结果。

senses.title: Officially in force
senses.definition: officially starting to apply, as a law, rule or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 法律、规则或协议等正式开始适用
senses.example: The ban is effective from 1 June.
senses.exampleCN: 该禁令自 6 月 1 日起生效。
senses.why: A rule that is in effect is effective: the same done thing, now described as having force.
senses.whyCN: in effect 的规则就是 effective：同一件做成之事，换了个说法强调它有力。

senses.title: Real in practice
senses.definition: existing or acting in fact, even if not officially recognized
senses.definitionCN: 事实上存在或起作用，即使未获正式承认
senses.example: She has effective control of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她对预算拥有实际控制权。
senses.why: What works in practice is real, so effective also means actual rather than nominal.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中起作用的就是真实的，因此 effective 也指实际上的，而非名义上的。

intro.en: Effective is effect plus the Latin adjective ending -ivus, which French passed on as -if.
intro.cn: effective 是 effect 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ivus，法语把它传成 -if。

items.en: Effectus, a thing done, supplied the noun stem for the adjective.
items.cn: effectus（做成之事）为形容词提供了名词词干。

items.en: Effectivus meant producing a result, and it named the power to bring something about.
items.cn: effectivus 意为「能产生结果的」，指促成某事的力量。

items.en: French effectif kept the sense of producing an effect and also of being real in fact.
items.cn: 法语 effectif 既保留「能产生效果」的意思，也指「事实上的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and used it for measures, medicines and rules.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用于措施、药物与规则。

items.en: The official-force sense settled in legal and business use, beside the practical sense.
items.cn: 「正式生效」一义在法律与商务用法中固定下来，与实践义并存。

entries.definition: A noun for a result, or a verb meaning to bring something about.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指结果，动词指使某事发生；effective 由它加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb of effective, meaning successfully or in practice.
entries.definitionCN: effective 的副词形式，义为「有效地」或「实际上」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being effective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，由 effective 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Working well without waste; it stresses economy of means rather than success alone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高效的」，强调不浪费，而不只是成功。

entries.definition: Producing the desired effect, used mostly of medicines and remedies; more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有功效的」，多用于药物与疗法，较正式。

entries.definition: Officially acceptable or legally in force, for documents and rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的、合法的」，多用于文件与规则。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow one key that fits: it opens the door, it is stamped by an office, and it works even when no one says so.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着一把对得上的钥匙：它开了门、被机关盖了章、没人说明也照样管用。

normal.en: Effective is effect plus -ive: able to leave the result you wanted.
normal.cn: effective 是 effect 加 -ive：有能力留下你想要的结果。

normal.en: A vaccine is effective if the illness does not take hold.
normal.cn: 疫苗有效，就是病没能扎下根。

normal.en: A law becomes effective on a date printed in the text.
normal.cn: 法律在文本里印着的那个日期生效。

normal.en: Effective control is control you actually have, not control on paper.
normal.cn: effective control 是你真正握着的控制权，不是纸面上的。

normal.en: Efficient is about no waste; effective is about the result arriving.
normal.cn: efficient 讲不浪费；effective 讲结果真的到了。

abstract.cn: 想象一把正好对上锁孔的钥匙。

abstract.en: The same key can open a door, carry an official stamp, or turn a budget.
abstract.cn: 同一把钥匙可以开门、可以带着公章，也可以转动一笔预算。

abstract.en: Effective means the result you aimed at is really there.
abstract.cn: effective 意味着你瞄准的结果真的在那里。

root: 由 effect 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；effect 又出自 efficere「做出、完成」，核心始终是「做出结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of effective: able to produce the wanted result, officially in force, and real in practice.
sensesIntro.cn: effective 的三个义项：能产生预期结果、正式生效、事实上成立。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key that meets its lock exactly, so the door opens at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把正好对上锁孔的钥匙，门一下就开了。

branches.en: THE RESULT: the key turns and the door really opens.
branches.cn: 结果线：钥匙一转，门真的开了。

branches.en: THE DATE: the same key is stamped to work from a fixed day.
branches.cn: 日期线：同一把钥匙被盖上章，从某天起生效。

branches.en: THE FACT: the key works even if no sign announces it.
branches.cn: 事实线：即使没有告示，钥匙照样起作用。

branches.en: THE TEST: both senses are proved by what actually happens.
branches.cn: 检验线：两个义项都由实际发生的事来证明。

branches.en: THE POWER: a measure can both work and be officially in force.
branches.cn: 效力线：一项措施既可以管用，也可以正式生效。

intro.en: Effective keeps the effect stem and adds Latin and French adjective endings; English then adds adverb and noun endings.
intro.cn: effective 保留 effect 词干，加上拉丁语与法语形容词词尾；英语随后再加副词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin effectus and effectivus are recorded, and French effectif is attested, so only the oldest layers are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 effectus 与 effectivus 均有记录，法语 effectif 也有书证，只有最古老的层次属于重构。

definition_zh: 有效地；实际上；几乎
definition_en: in a way that produces the intended result, in practice though not officially, or almost
core_image: 开关一按，机器立刻转起来——事情真的被推动了
scene: 雨越下越大，露天演出还没开始就被叫停了。The open-air show was effectively cancelled before it began.
sceneCN: 这里 effectively 是「实际上、等于」（第 2 个义项：虽未正式宣布，实际结果已经如此）；句意是露天演出还没开始就等于被取消了。

pos.zh: 副词：有效地；实际上；几乎

forms.label: 比较级（副词，多音节用 more）
最高级（副词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到，义为「有效的；生效的」
由 effective 加 -ness 构成，义为「有效性」
由 effective 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「无效的」

senses.title: In a way that succeeds
senses.definition: in a manner that produces the result intended
senses.definitionCN: 以能产生预期结果的方式
senses.example: The team communicated effectively during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机期间团队沟通得很有效。
senses.why: -ly turns effective into a manner: the result aimed at is actually reached.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把 effective 变成方式状语：瞄准的结果真的被达到了。

senses.title: In practice, though not officially
senses.definition: in effect or virtually, when the real situation is considered
senses.definitionCN: 从真实情况看已经如此，虽然并未正式宣布
senses.example: The old system was effectively dead by then.
senses.exampleCN: 到那时旧制度实际上已经死了。
senses.why: What is true in practice acts like a fact, so the adverb can mean virtually.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中成立的事就像事实一样起作用，所以这个副词可以表示「实际上、几乎」。

senses.title: Almost; practically
senses.definition: used before amounts or states to mean almost or for all practical purposes
senses.definitionCN: 用在数量或状态前，表示「几乎」或「就实际而言」
senses.example: The extra cost was effectively zero.
senses.exampleCN: 额外成本实际上几乎为零。
senses.why: If a quantity carries no practical weight, the adverb says it is almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个数量在实践中没有分量，这个副词就说它几乎等于没有。

intro.en: Effectively is English effective plus -ly; the stem itself goes back through French to Latin effectivus.
intro.cn: effectively 是英语 effective 加 -ly；词干本身经法语上溯到拉丁语 effectivus。

items.en: Effectus, a thing done, is the noun at the base of the family.
items.cn: effectus（做成之事）是整个词族底层的名词。

items.en: The adjective named the power to produce a result.
items.cn: 这个形容词指产生结果的力量。

items.en: French shortened the ending to -if and added the sense of being real.
items.cn: 法语把词尾简化为 -if，并加入「实际的」这一层意思。

items.en: English formed the adjective and used it for medicines, measures and laws.
items.cn: 英语构成这个形容词，用于药物、措施与法律。

items.en: The adverb -ly spread from manner into the looser sense of in practice.
items.cn: 副词 -ly 从「方式」扩展到更宽松的「实际上」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the effect family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of practical reality.
note.cn: 形近组收 effect 词族；近义组收表示「实际上」的副词。

entries.definition: Able to produce the wanted result, or officially in force.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的、生效的」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The quality of being effective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」。

entries.definition: A noun for a result or a verb meaning to bring something about.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指结果，动词指使某事发生。

entries.definition: In effect or almost, without being formally true.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上、几乎」，但并非正式成立。

entries.definition: Almost, or in practical terms rather than in theory.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「几乎」或「就实际而言」。

entries.definition: In essence, when the main point is considered.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「本质上、基本上」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a switch that works and then loosen into the everyday claim that something is as good as done.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一个真的管用的开关出发，再松到日常说法里「等于已经如此」。

normal.en: Effectively is effective plus -ly: the manner in which the result is reached.
normal.cn: effectively 是 effective 加 -ly：结果被达到的那种方式。

normal.en: A team that communicates effectively gets the message across the first time.
normal.cn: 有效沟通的团队一次就把话说到了。

normal.en: A cancelled show can be effectively cancelled before any sign is posted.
normal.cn: 一场演出可以在贴出告示之前就等于被取消了。

normal.en: Effectively zero means the cost is there on paper but weighs nothing.
normal.cn: effectively zero 指账面上有成本，实际却没有分量。

normal.en: The adverb moves from how you work to what is true in practice.
normal.cn: 这个副词从「你怎么做」滑到「实践上是什么样」。

abstract.en: Picture a switch pressed and a machine starting at once.
abstract.cn: 想象开关一按，机器立刻转起来。

abstract.en: The same press can be a good meeting, a dead system, or a cost near zero.
abstract.cn: 同一次按下可以是开好一场会、一个死掉的制度，或一笔近乎为零的成本。

abstract.en: Effectively means the result is already there, whether or not anyone announces it.
abstract.cn: effectively 意味着结果已经在那里，无论有没有人宣布。

examples.en: The team communicated effectively during the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机期间团队沟通得很有效。

examples.en: The old system was effectively dead by then.
examples.cn: 到那时旧制度实际上已经死了。

examples.en: The extra cost was effectively zero.
examples.cn: 额外成本实际上几乎为零。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of effectively: in a way that succeeds, in practice though not officially, and almost.
sensesIntro.cn: effectively 的三个义项：以有效的方式、实际上（虽未正式）、几乎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a switch pressed, and the machine starts at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：开关一按，机器立刻转起来。

chain: THE PLAIN WAY TO SAY IT

branches.en: THE MANNER: the work is done in a way that reaches the result.
branches.cn: 方式线：做事的方式真的达到了结果。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE: the situation is already so, without a formal word.
branches.cn: 实际线：没有正式说法，情况已经如此。

branches.en: THE AMOUNT: a quantity is there but weighs almost nothing.
branches.cn: 数量线：数量还在，却几乎没有分量。

branches.en: THE SLIDE: the same adverb slides from doing well to being almost nothing.
branches.cn: 滑动线：同一个副词从「做得好」滑到「几乎为零」。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: both loosen the statement to what is true in practice.
branches.cn: 判断线：两者都把话放松到「实践上成立」。

intro.en: Effectively is a transparent English build: the effect stem, an adjective ending, and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: effectively 是透明的英语构词：effect 词干、形容词词尾，再加副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun and adjective are recorded; English -ly is a native suffix, so nothing here needs reconstruction except the oldest root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词与形容词都有记录；英语 -ly 是本土词尾，因此除最古老词根外无需重构。

definition_zh: 效率；高效；效率比
definition_en: the quality of doing something well without waste, or the ratio of useful output to the energy or effort put in
core_image: 同样一桶油，跑得更远的那辆车
scene: 工厂换掉漏气的管道后，每吨产品的耗电降了一半。Engineers measured the gain in efficiency at every stage.
sceneCN: 这里 efficiency 是「效率」（第 1 个义项：有用产出与投入之比）；句意是工程师在每个环节测量效率的提升。

pos.zh: 名词：效率；高效；效率比

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ency 得到，义为「高效的」
由 efficient 加 -ly 构成，义为「高效地」
由 efficient 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效的」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效；效率低下」

senses.title: Output compared with input
senses.definition: the ratio of useful work or output to the energy, time or effort supplied
senses.definitionCN: 有用功或产出与所投入的能量、时间或努力之比
senses.example: The new engine raises fuel efficiency by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机把燃油效率提高了五分之一。
senses.why: Efficientia named the power of a cause to produce an effect; measured, that power becomes a ratio of output to input.
senses.whyCN: efficientia 指原因产生效果的力量；一旦被测量，这份力量就成为产出与投入之比。

senses.title: Working well without waste
senses.definition: the quality of doing something well with little waste of time, money or energy
senses.definitionCN: 把事情做好而很少浪费时间、金钱或精力的品质
senses.example: The office is known for its efficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 这个办公室以高效著称。
senses.why: A thing that produces its effect without waste is efficient, and the quality it shows is efficiency.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却能产生效果的东西是 efficient，而它显露出的这种品质就是 efficiency。

senses.title: A measured instance of such a ratio
senses.definition: a particular measurement or instance of efficient performance, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某一具体的效率测量结果或表现，常用复数
senses.example: The report compares the efficiencies of three plants.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了三家工厂的效率值。
senses.why: Once the ratio is counted, each count becomes a noun of its own, so the plural names separate figures.
senses.whyCN: 比值一旦被计数，每个计数就各自成为一个名词，于是复数指一项项分开的数字。

intro.en: Efficiency comes from Latin efficientia, the noun of efficere, through French efficience.
intro.cn: efficiency 来自拉丁语 efficientia（efficere 的名词），经法语 efficience 进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make, the base of the whole group.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是整个词组的词基。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to accomplish or bring about.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「完成、做出」。

items.en: Efficientia named the power or action of producing a result.
items.cn: efficientia 指产生结果的力量或作用。

items.en: French passed the noun on with the sense of power to produce an effect.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词传下来，保留「产生效果的力量」之义。

items.en: Engineering and economics turned the abstract power into a measured ratio.
items.cn: 工程学与经济学把这种抽象力量变成可测量的比值。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficient family; the near-meaning group separates productivity, economy and effectiveness.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficient 词族；近义组区分 productivity、economy 与 effectiveness。

entries.definition: Working well without waste of time or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高效的」，是本词的形容词词基。

entries.definition: In an efficient manner, without waste.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「高效地、不浪费地」。

entries.definition: The quality of producing the wanted result, whether or not means are spared.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只管结果是否达到，不管省不省。

entries.definition: Output per worker or per hour; efficiency measured in production.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生产率」，以产量衡量的效率。

entries.definition: Careful use of money and resources; the act of sparing rather than the ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节约」，指省用的行为，而不是比值。

entries.definition: The power to reach the intended result, without any claim about cost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只讲能否达到预期结果，不谈成本。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one tank of fuel and ask how far it carries the car, then widen to offices and whole plants.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一桶油能跑多远出发，再扩到办公室与整座工厂。

normal.en: Efficiency asks: how much useful work comes out of what you put in?
normal.cn: efficiency 问的是：投进去的东西产出了多少有用的功？

normal.en: The same tank of fuel, a longer drive: that is fuel efficiency.
normal.cn: 同一桶油跑得更远，这就是 fuel efficiency。

normal.en: An office with efficiency gets the work done and leaves the lights off.
normal.cn: 高效的办公室把活干完，还顺手把灯关掉。

normal.en: Efficiency is the ratio; efficiencies are the separate figures you compare.
normal.cn: efficiency 是比值；efficiencies 是你拿来比较的一项项数字。

normal.en: Efficient is the adjective, efficiency the quality it shows.
normal.cn: efficient 是形容词，efficiency 是它显露出的品质。

abstract.en: Picture one barrel of oil and two cars leaving the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象一桶油和两辆从同一条线出发的车。

abstract.en: The farther car turns the same barrel into more distance.
abstract.cn: 跑得更远的那辆车把同一桶油变成了更多里程。

abstract.en: Efficiency is that comparison written as a number.
abstract.cn: efficiency 就是把这种比较写成一个数字。

examples.en: The new engine raises fuel efficiency by a fifth.
examples.cn: 新发动机把燃油效率提高了五分之一。

examples.en: The office is known for its efficiency.
examples.cn: 这个办公室以高效著称。

examples.en: The report compares the efficiencies of three plants.
examples.cn: 报告比较了三家工厂的效率值。

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加 ex-「出」构成 efficere「完成」，其名词 efficientia 指「产生效果的力量」，经法语 efficience 进入英语，后转为可测量的产出投入之比。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficiency: the ratio of output to input, the quality of working without waste, and a measured instance of that ratio.
sensesIntro.cn: efficiency 的三个义项：产出与投入之比、不浪费地做好事情的品质，以及一项具体的效率测量值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one barrel of fuel carried farther by the better car.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一桶油，被更好的那辆车跑得更远。

branches.en: THE RATIO: useful output divided by what was put in.
branches.cn: 比值线：有用产出除以投入。

branches.en: THE HABIT: the work is done well and little is thrown away.
branches.cn: 习惯线：活干得好，扔掉的少。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: each measurement stands as its own count.
branches.cn: 数字线：每一次测量各自成为一项数字。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: a ratio only means something when figures are set side by side.
branches.cn: 比较线：比值只有把数字并排放在一起才有意义。

branches.en: THE SAVING: less waste is exactly what lifts the ratio.
branches.cn: 节约线：少浪费正是把比值抬上去的东西。

intro.en: Efficiency is a Latin-derived noun in -ency; English builds the adjective efficient and its adverb on the same stem.
intro.cn: efficiency 是以 -ency 收尾的拉丁语来源名词；英语在同一词干上构成形容词 efficient 及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin efficere and efficientia are recorded, so only the Indo-European base of facere is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 与 efficientia 均有记录，只有 facere 的印欧词基属于重构。

definition_zh: 高效的；能干的；有产生力的
definition_en: working well with little waste, organized and capable, or having the power to produce an effect
core_image: 一条流水线，零件进来，成品出去，地上没有剩料
scene: 换上新电机后，同样的活只用一半时间就干完了。The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
sceneCN: 这里 efficient 是「高效的」（第 1 个义项：以较少的投入完成同样的工作）；句意是新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

pos.zh: 形容词：高效的；能干的；有产生力的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ency 构成，义为「效率」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「高效地」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效的」

senses.title: Working without waste
senses.definition: working well and completely, with little waste of time, energy or materials
senses.definitionCN: 做事又好又完整，很少浪费时间、精力或材料
senses.example: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。
senses.why: Efficient is the Latin efficiens, doing or accomplishing: a thing that gets the work done without spending more than it must.
senses.whyCN: efficient 是拉丁语 efficiens，意为「正在做成的」：把活干成，却不比必须的多花一分。

senses.title: Organized and capable
senses.definition: of a person, organized and able to do a job well and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指人时，有条理、能把事情做好做快
senses.example: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。
senses.why: A person who finishes work without waste shows the same power to accomplish, so the adjective moves from machines to people.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却把活完成的人，显露的是同一种「做成」的力量，于是这个形容词从机器移到了人身上。

senses.title: Having the power to produce an effect
senses.definition: having the power to bring about a result, as in the technical phrase efficient cause
senses.definitionCN: 具有产生结果的力量，用于「动力因」这一术语
senses.example: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
senses.exampleCN: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply producing: an efficient cause is the doer that makes the effect exist.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「产生」：动力因是让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

intro.en: Efficient comes from Latin efficiens, the present participle of efficere, to accomplish, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: efficient 来自拉丁语 efficiens，即 efficere（完成）的现在分词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make and supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，提供这个动词的词基。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to work out or accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「做出、完成」。

items.en: The participle efficiens described something as accomplishing or producing.
items.cn: 分词 efficiens 描述某物正在完成或正在产生。

items.en: French passed the adjective on with the sense of producing a result.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传下来，意思是「能产生结果的」。

items.en: Industry added the everyday sense of working without waste of time or fuel.
items.cn: 工业又加入了日常义：不浪费时间或燃料地把活干好。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficiency family; the near-meaning group separates effective, productive and economical.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficiency 词族；近义组区分 effective、productive 与 economical。

entries.definition: The quality of working without waste, or the output-to-input ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效率」，即不浪费的品质或产出投入之比。

entries.definition: In a manner that wastes little time or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「高效地」，很少浪费时间或精力。

entries.definition: The power to reach the intended result, with no claim about waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只管结果达没达到，不管浪不浪费。

entries.definition: Producing the result wanted; it asks whether the aim is reached, not what it cost.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」，只问目标是否达到，不问成本。

entries.definition: Producing a good amount of work or goods; it stresses output.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多产的」，强调产出量。

entries.definition: Saving money or resources; it stresses the cost spared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的」，强调省下的花费。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line that leaves no scrap on the floor, then move to a tidy manager and to a cause that makes things happen.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一条地上没有剩料的流水线出发，再走到干练的经理与「让事情发生」的原因。

normal.en: Efficient means the same work with less fuel, less time and less scrap.
normal.cn: efficient 就是用更少的燃料、时间和废料完成同样的活。

normal.en: An efficient manager ends the meeting when the decision is made.
normal.cn: 能干的经理在决定做出时就结束会议。

normal.en: Efficient and effective are cousins: one saves, the other arrives.
normal.cn: efficient 与 effective 是表亲：一个讲省，一个讲结果到了。

normal.en: The old philosophical sense is plain: efficient cause means the doer.
normal.cn: 古老的哲学义很直白：efficient cause 就是那个施行者。

normal.en: Efficiency is the noun, efficiently the adverb, inefficient the opposite.
normal.cn: efficiency 是名词，efficiently 是副词，inefficient 是反义。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line with parts going in and products coming out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条工厂流水线，零件进去，成品出来。

abstract.en: Look at the floor: nothing usable is left lying there.
abstract.cn: 再看地面：没有还能用的东西被丢在那里。

abstract.en: Efficient is that picture of full output and empty waste.
abstract.cn: efficient 就是「产出满、废料空」的那幅图。

examples.en: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
examples.cn: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

examples.en: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
examples.cn: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。

examples.en: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
examples.cn: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊菲申特」——同一条流水线，地上没有剩料

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加 ex-「出」构成 efficere「完成」，其现在分词 efficiens 指「正在做成的」，经法语 efficient 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficient: working without waste, a person who is organized and capable, and the technical sense of producing an effect.
sensesIntro.cn: efficient 的三个义项：不浪费地把活干好、人干练有条理，以及「能产生结果」的术语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a production line with parts going in, products coming out, and no scrap on the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条流水线，零件进去，成品出来，地上没有剩料。

branches.en: THE SAVING: the same work is done with less fuel and less scrap.
branches.cn: 节省线：同样的活，用更少的燃料与废料完成。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a worker whose desk and schedule leave no waste.
branches.cn: 人物线：桌面与日程都不留浪费的工作者。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the doer that makes the result exist.
branches.cn: 原因线：让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

branches.en: THE POWER: both senses are about producing, one with economy and one in philosophy.
branches.cn: 力量线：两个义项都关乎「产生」，一个讲节省，一个讲哲学。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a person can be as efficient as a well-tuned machine.
branches.cn: 习惯线：人可以像调好的机器一样高效。

intro.en: Efficient carries the Latin participle ending -ens; English adds -ency, -ly and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: efficient 带着拉丁语分词词尾 -ens；英语再加 -ency、-ly 与否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.en: Latin efficere and efficiens are recorded, so only the Indo-European base of facere is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 与 efficiens 均有记录，只有 facere 的印欧词基属于重构。

definition_zh: 高效地；不浪费时间地；以高产出的方式
definition_en: in a way that uses little time or energy for the work done, by a well-planned method, or with high output for the input
core_image: 仓库里货架重排，取货的人少走一半路
scene: 仓库把货架重新排过，取货的人少走了一半的路。Goods now move efficiently from shelf to van.
sceneCN: 这里 efficiently 是「高效地」（第 1 个义项：用较少时间与力气完成同样的活）；句意是货物现在从货架到货车都走得很高效。

pos.zh: 副词：高效地；不浪费时间地；以高产出的方式

forms.label: 比较级（副词，多音节用 more）
最高级（副词，多音节用 most）

由 efficient 加 -ency 构成，义为「效率」
由 efficient 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效的」

senses.title: Without wasted effort
senses.definition: in a way that uses little time, energy or material for the work done
senses.definitionCN: 以较少的时间、精力或材料完成所做工作的方式
senses.example: Goods now move efficiently from shelf to van.
senses.exampleCN: 货物现在从货架到货车都走得很高效。
senses.why: -ly turns efficient into a manner: the work is finished and little is spent doing it.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把 efficient 变成方式：活干完了，而干的过程中花得很少。

senses.title: By a well-planned method
senses.definition: by an organized method in which each step follows the last without doubling back
senses.definitionCN: 以有条理的方法进行，每一步接上一步，不来回折返
senses.example: The whole event was efficiently run.
senses.exampleCN: 整场活动办得有条不紊。
senses.why: An organized schedule removes wasted motion, so efficiently also describes the order of the steps.
senses.whyCN: 有条理的日程去掉了多余的走动，所以 efficiently 也描述步骤的先后顺序。

senses.title: With high output for the input
senses.definition: of a machine or system, producing a large useful output compared with what is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或系统，与投入相比产出很多有用的东西
senses.example: The pump runs efficiently at low speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵在低速下也运转得很高效。
senses.why: For machines, doing well is measured as output over input, and the adverb reports that ratio.
senses.whyCN: 对机器来说，干得好要用产出除以投入来衡量，而这个副词报告的正是那个比值。

intro.en: Efficiently is English efficient plus -ly, with the stem going back through French to Latin efficiens.
intro.cn: efficiently 是英语 efficient 加 -ly，词干经法语上溯到拉丁语 efficiens。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「完成」。

items.en: The participle described something as accomplishing or producing.
items.cn: 分词描述某物正在完成或正在产生。

items.en: French kept the adjective with the sense of producing a result.
items.cn: 法语保留这个形容词，意思是「能产生结果的」。

items.en: English applied it to machines, methods and people who waste little.
items.cn: 英语把它用于机器、方法与很少浪费的人。

items.en: The adverb -ly carried the same idea into how an action is performed.
items.cn: 副词 -ly 把同一个意思带进「动作如何进行」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficiency family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of smooth and productive action.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficiency 词族；近义组收表示顺畅、多产地行动的副词。

entries.definition: Working well without waste, or able to produce a result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高效的」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The quality of working without waste, or the output-to-input ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效率」。

entries.definition: In a way that succeeds, or in practice; it stresses the result, not the saving.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有效地、实际上」，强调结果而不强调省。

entries.definition: Without trouble or interruption; it stresses flow rather than economy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「顺利地」，强调顺畅而非节省。

entries.definition: In a way that yields a good amount of work or output.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「多产地」，强调产出量。

entries.definition: In a way that saves money or resources.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「节约地」，强调省钱省资源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow a shorter walk in a warehouse, then a well-run day and a pump that gives more than it takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着仓库里缩短的一段路，再走到井井有条的一天与一台「产出多过消耗」的泵。

normal.en: Efficiently means fewer steps for the same delivery.
normal.cn: efficiently 就是用更少的步子完成同样的送货。

normal.en: A reordered shelf can cut a warehouse walk in half.
normal.cn: 重排一次货架，就能把仓库里的走动砍掉一半。

normal.en: An efficiently run event has no one waiting for someone else.
normal.cn: 办得有条理的活动，没有人干等另一个人。

normal.en: For a pump, efficiently means output divided by input.
normal.cn: 对泵来说，efficiently 就是产出除以投入。

normal.en: Efficient is what it is; efficiently is how it is done.
normal.cn: efficient 说的是它什么样；efficiently 说的是它怎么做。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse where every shelf sits where the picker turns first.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，每排货架都正好在取货人转身就能到的地方。

abstract.en: The goods travel the same distance in the end, but the walk is shorter.
abstract.cn: 货物最终走的距离没变，但人走的路短了。

abstract.en: Efficiently is that shorter walk written as an adverb.
abstract.cn: efficiently 就是把那段更短的路写成一个副词。

examples.en: Goods now move efficiently from shelf to van.
examples.cn: 货物现在从货架到货车都走得很高效。

examples.en: The whole event was efficiently run.
examples.cn: 整场活动办得有条不紊。

examples.en: The pump runs efficiently at low speeds.
examples.cn: 这台泵在低速下也运转得很高效。

root: 由 efficient 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；efficient 出自拉丁语 efficiens「正在做成的」，再往前是 efficere「完成」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficiently: without wasted effort, by a well-planned method, and with high output for the input.
sensesIntro.cn: efficiently 的三个义项：不浪费力气、按有条理的方法、以高产出对投入的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shelves reordered so the picker walks half as far.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架重排后，取货人少走一半路。

branches.en: THE WASTE: the same work costs less time and energy.
branches.cn: 浪费线：同样的活花费更少的时间与精力。

branches.en: THE ORDER: each step follows the one before without doubling back.
branches.cn: 顺序线：每一步接上一步，不来回折返。

branches.en: THE RATIO: a machine gives much for what is supplied.
branches.cn: 比值线：机器对投入给出很多。

branches.en: THE FLOW: a good order is itself the way waste is removed.
branches.cn: 流程线：好的顺序本身就是去掉浪费的方式。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: people and machines are judged by the same saving.
branches.cn: 衡量线：人和机器都用同一套节省标准来评判。

intro.en: Efficiently is a transparent English build on the Latin stem efficiens, closed by the native adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: efficiently 是在拉丁词干 efficiens 上的透明英语构词，末尾是本土副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin efficiens and efficere are recorded; the only reconstructed layer is the Indo-European base of facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 efficiens 与 efficere 均有记录，唯一属于重构的层次是 facere 的印欧词基。
