definition_zh: 努力；费力；尝试；成果；（集体的）行动
definition_en: the use of physical or mental energy, an attempt, a piece of work judged by its quality, or an organized campaign
core_image: 一根绳子被拉到最紧，掌心留下绳纹
scene: 他连着拉了十次绳子，帆才终于升到顶。It took a great effort to raise the sail.
sceneCN: 这里 effort 是「力气、努力」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神上的用力）；句意是升起船帆费了很大力气。

pos.zh: 名词：努力；费力；尝试；成果；集体行动

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -less 构成，义为「毫不费力的」
由 effortless 加 -ly 构成，义为「毫不费力地」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「费力的」

senses.title: Physical or mental exertion
senses.definition: the use of energy, strength or thought in order to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而付出的精力、力气或心思
senses.example: It took a great effort to raise the sail.
senses.exampleCN: 升起船帆费了很大力气。
senses.why: Effort comes from a French verb meaning to force or strengthen: it is strength put out on purpose.
senses.whyCN: effort 来自一个意为「用力、使强壮」的法语动词：它是有意拿出来的力气。

senses.title: An attempt
senses.definition: an act of trying to do something, especially when success is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 试图做成某事的行动，尤指结果并不确定时
senses.example: He made one last effort to reach the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他拼尽最后一番努力想游到岸边。
senses.why: A burst of strength aimed at a goal is also a try, so effort names the attempt itself.
senses.whyCN: 朝目标爆发的一股力气也是一次尝试，于是 effort 也指尝试本身。

senses.title: A piece of work judged by its quality
senses.definition: a particular attempt or achievement, often judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 某一次尝试或成果，常被评价为好或差
senses.example: Her first novel was a fine effort.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说是部不错的作品。
senses.why: What has been produced by exerted strength can stand as the work itself, so the effort is the result.
senses.whyCN: 用力之后产出的东西可以当作作品本身，于是这份努力就成了成果。

senses.title: An organized campaign
senses.definition: a coordinated attempt by a group of people, often for aid, rescue or change
senses.definitionCN: 一群人协调一致的行动，常指援助、救援或推动改变
senses.example: The relief effort reached the village by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在中午前抵达了村子。
senses.why: Many people putting out strength together form one shared effort, so the word can name a whole campaign.
senses.whyCN: 许多人一起把力气拿出来，汇成一份共同的努力，于是这个词可以指整场行动。

intro.en: Effort comes from Old French esforz, from the verb esforcier, to force or strengthen, and goes back to Latin fortis, strong.
intro.cn: effort 来自古法语 esforz，源自动词 esforcier（用力、使强壮），更早追溯到拉丁语 fortis（强壮的）。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, and it is the root of force and effort alike.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮的」，是 force 与 effort 共同的根。

items.en: Fortia named strength or force, the quality that can be put out.
items.cn: fortia 指力量或强力，即可以被拿出来的那种品质。

items.en: The verb meant to force, strengthen or exert oneself.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「使劲、加强、竭力」。

items.en: The noun named an exertion, a striving or a feat of strength.
items.cn: 名词指一次用力、一番拼搏或一场力量之举。

items.en: English borrowed it for the act of trying hard and later for the attempt itself.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示「努力去做」，后来又指尝试本身。

items.en: The sense of a shared campaign grew from many people exerting themselves together.
items.cn: 「共同行动」一义由许多人一起用力的情形发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on effort; the near-meaning group separates attempt, exertion and endeavor.
note.cn: 形近组收由 effort 构成的词；近义组区分 attempt、exertion 与 endeavor。

entries.definition: Needing no effort; formed from effort with -less.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫不费力的」，由 effort 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no effort; effortless plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「毫不费力地」，由 effortless 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Requiring noticeable effort; effort plus -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「费力的」，由 effort 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: An act of trying; it names the try more than the strength spent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「尝试」，更强调「试」而不是花掉多少力气。

entries.definition: Hard physical or mental work; it stresses the strain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「费力、劳累」，强调承受的紧张。

entries.definition: A serious attempt or undertaking; more formal and more purposeful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「努力、事业」，更正式、更有目标感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow one rope pulled tight, then a last try, then a finished piece and a shared rescue.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着一根拉紧的绳子，再走到最后一次尝试、一件成品与一场共同救援。

normal.en: Effort is strength put out on purpose.
normal.cn: effort 就是有意拿出来的力气。

normal.en: The rope leaves its mark on the palm: that mark is effort.
normal.cn: 绳子在掌心留下纹路：那道纹就是 effort。

normal.en: One last pull can be both an effort and an attempt.
normal.cn: 最后一把拉，既是一份力气，也是一次尝试。

normal.en: A fine effort is a piece of work you judge, not a muscle you measure.
normal.cn: a fine effort 是你评价的作品，不是你测量的肌肉。

normal.en: A relief effort is many people's strength gathered into one campaign.
normal.cn: relief effort 是许多人的力气汇成一场行动。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled until it hums.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被拉到发出嗡响。

abstract.en: The same pull can be a try, a finished work, or a village rescue.
abstract.cn: 同一次拉，可以是一次尝试、一件成品，或一场村庄救援。

abstract.en: Effort is what it costs to move something that does not move by itself.
abstract.cn: effort 就是推动一个自己不会动的东西所要付出的代价。

examples.en: It took a great effort to raise the sail.
examples.cn: 升起船帆费了很大力气。

examples.en: He made one last effort to reach the shore.
examples.cn: 他拼尽最后一番努力想游到岸边。

examples.en: The relief effort reached the village by noon.
examples.cn: 救援行动在中午前抵达了村子。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of effort: exertion, an attempt, a piece of work judged by quality, and an organized campaign.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled tight, leaving its mark on the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子被拉到最紧，掌心留下绳纹。

branches.en: THE STRAIN: energy of body or mind put into the work.
branches.cn: 用力线：身体或心思被投进工作里的能量。

branches.en: THE TRY: the same burst of strength aimed at a goal.
branches.cn: 尝试线：同一股力气朝着目标使出去。

branches.en: THE WORK: what the strength produced, judged as good or poor.
branches.cn: 成果线：力气产出的东西，被评好或评差。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: many people's strength gathered into one action.
branches.cn: 行动线：许多人的力气汇成一次行动。

branches.en: ONE PULL: every attempt begins with strength deliberately spent.
branches.cn: 同一把拉：每次尝试都从有意花掉的力气开始。

intro.en: Effort is a French noun in -t built on a verb of forcing; English adds -less, -ful and -ly.

definition_en: the oval body laid by a female bird, a female reproductive cell, or to urge someone on
core_image: 一只蛋落进沸水，蛋白很快凝成白色
scene: 清晨的锅里，水一开，壳里的东西很快凝成白色。She cracked an egg into the boiling water.
sceneCN: 这里 egg 是「蛋」（第 1 个义项：雌鸟产下的、带壳的椭圆体，可作食物）；句意是她把一只蛋磕进沸水里。

pos.zh: 名词：蛋；卵；卵细胞

senses.title: The body laid by a female bird
senses.definition: the oval object with a shell that a female bird lays, eaten as food or hatched into a chick
senses.definitionCN: 雌鸟产下的带壳椭圆体，可作食物，也可孵出小鸟
senses.example: She cracked an egg into the boiling water.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一只蛋磕进沸水里。
senses.why: The noun came from Old Norse egg, the everyday word for the shelled body a bird lays.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自古诺尔斯语 egg，就是鸟产下的那个带壳物体的日常说法。

senses.title: A female reproductive cell
senses.definition: the ovum, the cell produced by a female that joins with a sperm in reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 雌性产生、在生殖中与精子结合的细胞，即卵细胞
senses.example: Each egg carries half of the genetic material.
senses.exampleCN: 每个卵细胞携带一半的遗传物质。
senses.why: The bird's egg is one cell writ large, so biology uses the same word for the ovum.
senses.whyCN: 鸟蛋就是一个被放大的细胞，因此生物学用同一个词指卵细胞。

senses.title: To urge someone on
senses.definition: to encourage someone to do something, often something risky or foolish
senses.definitionCN: 鼓励某人去做某事，常指冒险或不明智的事
senses.example: His friends egged him on to jump.
senses.exampleCN: 他的朋友们怂恿他跳下去。
senses.why: This verb is a different word: Old English eggian meant to incite, and it merely shares the spelling of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是另一个词：古英语 eggian 意为「煽动」，只是与名词拼写相同。

intro.en: The noun egg came from Old Norse, while the verb egg on came separately from Old English eggian; the two are unrelated despite the shared spelling.
intro.cn: 名词 egg 来自古诺尔斯语，动词 egg on 则另出自古英语 eggian；两者拼写相同，来源却无关。

items.en: Old Norse egg named the shelled body laid by a bird, and it replaced the older English word.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 egg 指鸟产下的带壳之物，并取代了英语原有的说法。

items.en: Middle English kept the Norse word for the food and the hatchable body.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个诺尔斯语词，指食物与可孵化的卵。

items.en: A separate verb eggian meant to incite or provoke, and it survives only in egg on.
items.cn: 另一个动词 eggian 意为「煽动、挑动」，只存活在 egg on 这一短语里。

items.en: The noun widened from the bird's egg to the ovum and to egg as food.
items.cn: 名词从鸟蛋扩展到卵细胞，也固定为食物意义上的蛋。

items.en: The homographs now sit in one dictionary entry, though their histories never met.
items.cn: 这两个同形词如今列在同一词条里，但它们的历史从未相遇。

normal.en: An egg is a shell with a cell inside, and both meanings grow from that.

normal.en: Crack it into boiling water and the white sets at once.
normal.cn: 磕进沸水里，蛋白立刻凝住。

normal.en: In biology the same word shrinks to the single cell.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，同一个词缩小成那一个细胞。

normal.cn: egg on 与名词无关：它是一个表示「煽动」的古动词。

normal.en: Eggshell, eggy and eggless all keep the noun's plain shape.
normal.cn: eggshell、eggy、eggless 都保留名词的朴素词形。

abstract.cn: 想象同一个椭圆形状出现在三个不同地方。

abstract.en: In a pan it is breakfast, under a microscope it is a cell, in a shout it is a dare.
abstract.cn: 在锅里是早餐，在显微镜下是细胞，在一声喊里是挑动。

abstract.en: Egg is one shape with two histories that only share a spelling.
abstract.cn: egg 是一个形状带着两段历史，而这两段只共用拼写。

sensesIntro.cn: egg 的三个义项：鸟产下的带壳卵、雌性生殖细胞，以及同形异源、表示「怂恿」的动词。

senses.title: The number eight
senses.definition: the number 8, the quantity that comes after seven
senses.definitionCN: 数字 8，排在七之后的那个数量
senses.example: There are eight windows on this floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这一层有八扇窗。
senses.why: Eight is the inherited Germanic numeral, from a root shared with octopus and October; it names the count itself.
senses.whyCN: eight 是继承下来的日耳曼语数词，与 octopus、October 共用同一个古老词根；它命名的就是那个数量。

senses.title: A group of eight people
senses.definition: a set or team of eight people, especially the crew of a rowing boat
senses.definitionCN: 由八人组成的一组或一队，尤指赛艇的八人艇员
senses.example: The eight won the race by a length.
senses.exampleCN: 那条八人艇以一个艇身的优势赢了比赛。
senses.why: A crew is named by how many row it, so the numeral turns into a noun for the whole set of eight.
senses.whyCN: 一支赛艇队按划桨人数来称呼，于是这个数词变成一个名词，指八个人整体。

senses.title: The hour of eight o'clock
senses.definition: eight o'clock, used when telling the time
senses.definitionCN: 八点整，用于报时
senses.example: The train leaves at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 火车八点开。
senses.why: A clock face counts hours with the same numerals, so eight can stand for the eighth hour of the day.
senses.whyCN: 钟面用同一套数字来数小时，于是 eight 可以指一天中的第八个小时。

intro.en: Eight goes back to Old English eahta, from Proto-Germanic ahto and the same Indo-European root that gave octopus and October.
intro.cn: eight 上溯到古英语 eahta，源自原始日耳曼语 ahto，与 octopus、October 共用同一个印欧词根。

items.en: The reconstructed Indo-European root oktō meant eight.
items.cn: 重构的印欧词根 oktō 意为「八」。

items.en: Germanic kept the numeral as ahto, the form behind English eight.
items.cn: 日耳曼语把这个数词保留为 ahto，正是英语 eight 背后的形式。

items.en: Old English eahta was the everyday numeral and the base of the teen and ordinal forms.
items.cn: 古英语 eahta 是日常数词，也是「十几」形式与序数形式的词基。

items.en: Middle English kept the numeral and settled the modern spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个数词，并固定了现代拼写。

items.en: The cardinal stayed eight while the ordinal eighth and the teen forms branched off.
items.cn: 基数词保持 eight，而序数 eighth 与「十几」形式各自分支出去。

senses.title: The number eighteen
senses.definition: the number 18, the quantity between seventeen and nineteen
senses.definitionCN: 数字 18，介于十七与十九之间的数量
senses.example: Eighteen students signed up for the course.
senses.exampleCN: 有十八名学生报名了这门课。

senses.whyCN: eighteen 就是八加十：一个古老的复合词，直接数出一个数量。

senses.title: A set of eighteen holes

senses.example: A full round here means eighteen holes.

senses.why: A golf round is fixed at eighteen holes, so the number becomes the name of the whole round.
senses.whyCN: 一轮高尔夫固定为十八洞，于是这个数字成了整轮比赛的名称。

senses.title: The age of eighteen
senses.definition: the age at which a person is legally considered an adult in many countries

senses.example: She moved out at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十八岁那年搬了出去。
